conventions.evidence: Deviates from several explicit conventions: hardcoded UI strings in `resources/views/livewire/entity/dashboard.blade.php:3` ("Welcome to the entity dashboard."), `members.blade.php:7` ("Add"), `settings.blade.php:9,13,15,18,22,26` instead of `lang/*/ui.php`; domain writes (`Settings::delete/transfer`, `Members::addMember/removeMember`) live inline in Livewire instead of `app/Actions/*`; `app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:22-24` use no `#[Validate]`; the new `app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php` is an unused parallel registration mechanism. Some things do comply: reversible `down()` methods, `$this->authorize` in `mount()`, policies in `app/Policies/`.

security.evidence: Exploitable gaps: `app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:28-45` `addMember()` performs no authorization at all (task requires employees to get 403); `app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:21` exposes `public Entity $entity` without `#[Locked]` while `save()` (`:34`), `delete()` (`:51`) and `transfer()` (`:68`) never call `$this->authorize`, so a tampered `entity` id lets a user edit/delete another entity; `app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:59` and `:71` resolve `findOrFail($membershipId)` without scoping to `$this->entity`, so IDs from other entities are accepted. `app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:28` compares the enum cast to a string, so the owner-membership deletion guard is dead.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all (no `tests/Feature` or `tests/Unit` entries); conventions require every feature to ship with tests, including unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each Livewire action.

simplicity.evidence: No speculative layers, but plenty of avoidable code: duplicate `use App\Models\Entity;` in `app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:5,7` and `app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:5,7`, unused imports (`app/Models/Entity.php:11`, `app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:14`, `app/Http/Controllers/EntityPickController.php:11`), the dead `app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php`, and copy-pasted audit-log blocks in every action.

issues.explanation: Both files import `App\Models\Entity` twice, which is a PHP fatal error ("Cannot use ... because the name is already in use"), so neither component can be loaded.
`$user = \` followed by more backslashes is a PHP parse error (`syntax error, unexpected token "\"`), so the Members component cannot be compiled.

The routes use `Entity\Dashboard::class`, `Entity\Members::class` and `Entity\Settings::class`, which resolve to the nonexistent `Entity\...` namespace (the imports alias `Dashboard`, not `Entity`), so all three page routes fail; the imported classes are also unused.

`virtualAs('role = "owner" ? 1 : NULL')` uses a C-style ternary that is invalid SQL on both SQLite and MariaDB, and `virtualAs` creates a VIRTUAL column although the task requires a stored generated column; the migration cannot run on either target database.
`$membership->role !== UserRole::Admin->value` compares a `UserRole` enum instance to a string, so it is always true and `transfer()` always aborts with 403 — ownership transfer can never succeed.
`$currentOwner` may be null when the owner row has vanished, and `$currentOwner->role` then throws instead of returning the 403 the task requires.
`addMember()` never calls `$this->authorize(...)`, so any member (including an employee) can add users, violating the requirement that employees get 403 on add.

`public Entity $entity` is not `#[Locked]` and `save()`, `delete()` and `transfer()` do not re-authorize, so a client that tampers with the entity id can rename, delete or transfer ownership of an entity they are not the owner of.

`Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\HandlesAuthorization` does not exist (the trait is `Illuminate\Auth\Access\HandlesAuthorization`), so loading either policy is a fatal error and every `$this->authorize`/`@can` call fails.

The provider extends the nonexistent `Illuminate\Foundation\Support\ServiceProvider` and calls `registerPolicies()`, which that base class does not define; it is also not registered in `bootstrap/providers.php`, so policy registration does not happen.

`$membership->role === UserRole::Owner->value` compares the enum-cast value to a string and is always false, so the owner-removal guard never fires and an owner can remove their own membership (or be removed), leaving the entity without an owner.
Neither model defines `$fillable`/`#[Fillable]`, so `Settings::save()`'s `update([...])` and `memberships()->create([...])` throw `MassAssignmentException` with Laravel's default guarded attributes.

The model imports `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\HasFactory` and `...\Attributes\SoftDeletes` and uses them as traits; these are not the framework's `HasFactory`/`SoftDeletes` traits, so soft deletes are not applied (and the class likely fatals on the missing trait).

Action parameters are resolved with a global `findOrFail($membershipId)` and authorized against the membership's own entity, not `$this->entity`, so a manager of one entity can mutate memberships belonging to another entity where they also have rights.
`assignRole()` accepts the entity owner's membership id, so an admin can demote the owner to employee and leave the entity with zero owners (the DB unique index only forbids a second owner).

`{{ $membership->role }}` and `$membership->role === $role->value` treat the enum-cast attribute as a string; rendering an enum through `e()` throws, and the disabled state/comparisons are always wrong.
The factory defines only `role`, so it never creates the related entity and user the task requires ("creates its entity and user"), and inserts fail on the non-nullable foreign keys.
Only the `owner()` and `admin()` states are defined; the required `employee()` state is missing.

The task requires the `exists:users,email` validation rule, but only `email:strict` is declared and existence is checked manually afterwards, producing a hand-made `validation.exists` error instead of a field rule.
The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests, so none of the required happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper cases are covered.

Screen text is hardcoded in English ("Welcome to the entity dashboard.", "Add", "Remove", "Save", "Delete Entity", "Select new owner", "Transfer", "(Admin)") instead of coming from `lang/*/ui.php` as the task requires.

Domain writes (entity delete, ownership transfer, member add/remove/role change) are implemented inline in the components instead of `app/Actions/*` classes with authorization inside, which is the project's required pattern.

Public `$name`, `$slug` and `$targetMembershipId` carry no `#[Validate]`; validation is inline only in `save()`, and `$targetMembershipId` is never validated at all, contrary to the Livewire convention.
`mount()` only authorizes `view`, so the page is reachable by every member; the manager-only restriction for add/assign is not enforced during mount.
Unused/self-namespace imports, a misplaced docblock, an over-indented property and missing trailing newlines in the Blade files add noise and look unpolished.
The docs update only adds comments and drops the `UK` marker instead of documenting the new columns/indexes, and `CHANGELOG.md`/`docs/business-rules.md` were not updated as the conventions require.

review.summary: The change adds the entity data model, policies, factories, migrations, Livewire dashboard/members/settings pages and routes, but it does not run: two components have duplicate-import fatals, Members has a parse error, the routes point at a nonexistent class, the policies import a nonexistent trait, and the single-owner generated column uses invalid SQL. Beyond the breakage, `addMember()` is unauthenticated, the settings entity is not locked or re-authorized on actions, the owner guards are dead due to enum/string comparisons, and no tests are included, so this needs a full rework rather than a merge.
